title: On Pouring the water over the steps
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：pour　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pour 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the director ① poured the water over the steps with great care, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the director ② pours the water over the steps on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ pour the water over the steps at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ poured the water over the steps before — a line in the poster for August 1982 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Pouring the water over the steps with great care, the director said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ pour down the lane in a flood on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Pour down the lane in a flood at once and never mention it again.

By 1995 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the poster, and a new actor from the next theatre ⑧ pours down the lane in a flood with great care every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stage, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ poured the water over the steps again when nobody else would.

⑩ To pour the water over the steps, my mother said in 2000, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the theatre remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the theatre forgets, somebody pours the water over the steps on the same day again and somebody must pour the water over the steps with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 倾倒（一般过去式 poured the water over the steps：1988 年导演头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 倾倒（一般现在 pours the water over the steps：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 倾倒（不定式 to pour the water over the steps：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 倾倒（过去完成时 had poured the water over the steps：1982 年八月的戏报上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 倾倒（动名词 pouring the water over the steps 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 涌出（pour down the lane in a flood：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去涌出化作一股大水涌进那条小巷）
G. v. 涌出（pour down the lane in a flood：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 倾倒（后段两处：新来的演员照例 pours down the lane in a flood，而母亲又一次 poured the water over the steps）

answers.why: pour 意为“倾倒”，1988 年导演小心翼翼地倾倒把水泼在台阶上，那是戏院里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 poured。
pour 意为“倾倒”，自那以后导演当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 pours。
pour 意为“倾倒”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯倾倒把水泼在台阶上”，此处为不定式 to pour the water over the steps。
pour 意为“倾倒”，戏报里 八月 那行字说明早在 1995 年之前就有人倾倒过，故用过去完成时 had poured。
pour 意为“倾倒”，导演说“倾倒把水泼在台阶上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 pouring the water over the steps 作主语。
pour 意为“涌出”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去涌出化作一股大水涌进那条小巷”，should ever 之后用原形 pour down the lane in a flood。
pour 意为“涌出”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻涌出化作一股大水涌进那条小巷（pour down the lane in a flood at once），以后再也不要提起。
pour 意为“倾倒”，新来的演员每个夜晚都照例涌出化作一股大水涌进那条小巷，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 pours。
pour 意为“倾倒”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地倾倒把水泼在台阶上，用一般过去式 poured 叙述。
pour 意为“倾倒”，结尾那句是母亲 2000 年的话：要倾倒把水泼在台阶上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和戏院记住的那一件。

早在 1982 年就有人倾倒把水泼在台阶上，八月那天戏报上的一行字就是证据。（had poured the water over the steps）
导演说过，小心翼翼地倾倒把水泼在台阶上这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（pouring the water over the steps 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻涌出化作一股大水涌进那条小巷，以后再也不要提起。（pour down the lane in a flood，祈使句）
answers: In 1988 the director poured the water over the steps with great care, and every actor in the theatre said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three nights on, the director still pours the water over the steps on the same day without being asked.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 pour 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1988 the director poured the water over the steps with great care, and nobody in the theatre forgot it.
Even now the director pours the water over the steps on the same day whenever the theatre asks.
Pouring the water over the steps with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever pour down the lane in a flood on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new actor from the next theatre pours down the lane in a flood with great care every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother poured the water over the steps again, and the theatre remembered that half.
